## Published reproduction and scope

This is a compatibility/semantic improvement to the package's intentional denylist design, **not a regression claim about the earlier symmetric-related fix**.

Tested official `pm-gantt-chart@2026.10.10`, npm gitHead/current main `1838ce4f2ea2aaf50858e7d36d9fb5e480cffc9b`, with installed `@unbrained/pm-cli@2026.10.12`, Node 24.19.0, Linux. Downloaded artifact matches npm SHA-1 and SHA-512. All examples use synthetic items; no service, model, or provider calls.

The host's [dependency-kind contract](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/docs/DEPENDENCY_KIND_CONTRACT.md) defines `A --blocks--> B` as B waiting for A, inverse to `B --blocked_by--> A`; implementation/association/provenance are distinct from ordering. Gantt instead treats every kind absent from its denylist as an item-to-prerequisite edge.

## Minimal public API reproduction

```js
import { computeSchedule, detectCycles } from "pm-gantt-chart";
const item = (id, dependencies = []) => ({
  id, title: id, type: "Task", status: "open",
  estimated_minutes: 480, dependencies
});
for (const kind of ["related", "implements", "blocked_by", "blocks"]) {
  const rows = [item("a", [{ id: "b", kind }]), item("b")];
  console.log(kind, Object.fromEntries(
    computeSchedule(rows, new Date("2026-10-12T00:00:00Z"), 1)
  ));
}
console.log(detectCycles([
  item("a", [{ id: "b", kind: "blocks" }]),
  item("b", [{ id: "a", kind: "blocked_by" }])
]));
```

Actual starts:
- `related`: A Oct 12, B Oct 12 (passing non-ordering control)
- `blocked_by`: A Oct 13, B Oct 12 (passing ordering control)
- `implements`: A Oct 13, B Oct 12; expected neither ordered by this edge
- `blocks`: A Oct 13, B Oct 12; expected A Oct 12, B Oct 13
- Equivalent inverse rows return a two-node cycle, although they express the same single ordering constraint

Additional API probes show `recurs_from` and `incident_from` also order work under the current denylist. They were not exercised through the installed CLI.

## Installed CLI confirmation and controls

Created independent two-item synthetic trackers through the current public SDK: Task `ga-a`, Decision `ga-b`, each estimated at 480 minutes. Installed the official package locally. On each tracker ran, in three separate processes:

```sh
pm gantt export --format json --schedule --from 2026-10-12 --output chart.json
```

All 18 executions were stable:
- Related-only: exit 0; both starts Oct 12; no exported prerequisites
- Implements-only: exit 0; ga-a starts Oct 13 and JSON reports `deps:["ga-b"]`
- Blocked-by-only: exit 0; ga-b Oct 12 then ga-a Oct 13
- Blocks-only: exit 0; same wrong direction as blocked-by
- Equivalent inverse rows: exit 2, zero stdout, no output file; falsely claims a fatal scheduling cycle
- Genuine blocked-by cycle: exit 2, zero stdout, no output file (passing fail-closed control)

Package/tracker/history file hashes, excluding runtime files, stayed unchanged by the export runs. Successful JSON files were 1,281 bytes for related and 1,303 for the other single-edge cases. This is bounded semantic acceptance, not full-suite, cross-platform, performance, or agent-autonomy certification.

## Existing ownership and requested direction

[Closed pm-gantt-chart-k8wm](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/1838ce4f2ea2aaf50858e7d36d9fb5e480cffc9b/.agents/pm/issues/pm-gantt-chart-k8wm.toon) / [PR #57](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/pull/57) intentionally fixed known non-gating spellings while leaving the wider denylist design for a separate change/review. Its notes explicitly acknowledge implements/blocks still gate. Preserve that provenance and the passing related behavior.

All 97 canonical PM items and all 134 GitHub issue/PR records, open and closed, were checked October 12. No current matching open follow-up was found. [Context #136](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/issues/136) is related semantic work in a different package, not the Gantt owner.

## Acceptance

- Derive a normalized prerequisite graph from authoritative registry ordering semantics, including inverse direction; avoid another growing hard-coded denylist
- Use that same graph for scheduling, cycle detection, critical path, slack, and exported prerequisites
- Deduplicate equivalent forward/inverse constraints so they do not form a false cycle
- Non-ordering association, implementation, provenance, and temporal links remain available as context without inventing dates or blocking chart generation
- Test the cases above through public API and installed CLI, retain true-cycle fail-closed behavior, and add registered custom ordering/non-ordering kinds and mixed-direction corpora
- Keep tracker data/history read-only; no implicit migration or relationship relabeling

Impact: agents can receive invented sequencing, reversed schedules, or a refusal to render a valid tracker.
Use registry ordering semantics for Gantt schedules and inverse-edge cycle detection

value.text: Published reproduction: ran the issue public API snippet unchanged against official pm-gantt-chart@2026.10.10 with @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.10.12 and Node 24.19.0. related starts both items October 12; blocked_by correctly starts a October 13 after b October 12. implements incorrectly delays a to October 13; blocks incorrectly has the same direction as blocked_by. Equivalent a blocks b / b blocked_by a reports a false two-node cycle. Tarball npm receipt: SHA-1 c1edd221be472075eac8b169d22e339b5ba61cea. Import search found no existing owner; pm-github has no number/limit filter, so a gated atomic timestamp-filtered preview and import each selected exactly issue 135, with gh:unbraind/pm-gantt-chart#135 provenance. No other issues imported.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Design: replace the denylist with one normalized item-to-prerequisite graph using the active SDK relationship registry ordering flag and precedence. Deduplicate inverse and provenance-distinct constraints; preserve original item relationships in memory and all tracker/history bytes. Scheduling, cycles, critical path, slack and CSV/JSON exports consume the graph. Missing kinds retain legacy blocked_by behavior; unknown kinds remain contextual. Raise peer/manifest minimum to verified 2026.10.6 so registry APIs are enforced at activation; preserve closed pm-gantt-chart-k8wm ownership and its related-link behavior. Add real SDK-created tracker and installed-tarball CLI coverage plus custom kind registration and mixed-direction API corpora.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Installed published CLI reproduction completed: independent two-item Task/Decision scratch trackers created through the public SDK, both estimated_minutes=480; ran the exact scheduled JSON export command three separate times per scenario (18 total). related and blocked_by controls pass; implements delays a incorrectly; blocks incorrectly delays a rather than b; equivalent inverse rows falsely exit 2 with zero stdout and no output; a genuine blocked_by cycle still exits 2. Durable tracker, history and installed-package hashes remain unchanged by exports. The initial fixture used an unrecognized estimate option; corrected via the typed estimatedMinutes SDK field before recording these final results.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Custom-kind integration findings: PM SDK 2026.10.6 activates and publishes registered custom relationship kinds, but native create/update dependency input still rejects those names against a built-in-only allowed list. Also, package-local registry resolution and the injected client contracts read omit active custom definitions in an installed extension. Reproduced through real scratch projects; do not change upstream here. Gantt resolves an explicit workspace SDK client, gets the authoritative registered ordering census, and supplements built-in constraints using full one-hop native predecessor queries for custom ordering kinds. Synthetic custom CLI fixtures explicitly seed registered storage spellings and restore setup bytes afterward; exports themselves remain observational. No migrations or relabeling are added to package behavior.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Both findings are valid. Missing relationship_kind_contracts now selects zero custom definitions and retains built-in ordering. The pinned SDK graph signature accepts one id/target and exposes no multi-root predecessor batch, so queries use bounded batches of four and merge results in corpus order. All roots remain necessary for incoming source-before-target constraints; filtering only stored custom dependencies would lose successor prerequisites. Real-tracker coverage includes an omitted census, more than four roots, incoming custom constraints and self-cycles; instrumentation forwards real graph calls unchanged to verify overlap and the concurrency limit. Current origin/main is already incorporated.
